deliberately_left_judged.item: 0231's own header/body comments not edited (A9's and A13's prose land in packages/db/README.md instead)
deliberately_left_judged.why: Independently confirmed both halves of the stated constraint: (1) migration 0231 is applied on clara_659 today (select version from clara.schema_migrations where version='0231_firm_portfolio_pack' returns a row); (2) packages/db/scripts/migrate.mjs:335-336 does contain the checksum-drift refusal cited ('applied migration ... was MODIFIED after being applied (checksum drift). Migrations are immutable -- add a new migration file instead'), and this repo already keeps a precedent section in README.md for exactly this situation (the pre-existing 0214 paragraph, confirmed present immediately above the new A9/A13 paragraphs). Editing the migration file in place would either be a no-op (if the DB rejects the drifted checksum) or would falsify the sha256(prosrc) pins other batteries assert against; writing the correction in README.md is the same move this codebase already made once.

ratification_requested_judged.item: Publish work_id on list_review_queue's work_question_rows (the real fix for A1)
ratification_requested_judged.why: DECISIONS.md row 0231 (#659's own row) states 'Recuts: none' in its own column, confirmed by direct grep of the live file. A recut of clara.list_review_queue (a different, unrelated migration's function) to add a column is categorically a recut this ticket's row forbids, not a scope call the fix-round worker could make unilaterally. The chosen alternative (withdraw the link to its pre-#659 fall-through, name the residual, leave a live db-level tripwire cell) is precisely option (a) the adversarial review itself offered as an acceptable fix, not an invention. No action needed from this recheck beyond flagging it to the orchestrator, which the fixround report already does explicitly.
